scope: host-owned campaign state, class-specific experience, deterministic authored-event selection, unique-item quality, legacy saves, and custom-only multiplayer

source_evidence.observation: The normal build defines four player slots; a conditional build can define eight.
source_evidence.constraint: Campaign V1 fixes capacity at four until the four-player runtime gate passes.

source_evidence.observation: Join validates executable VERSION and, for legacy multiplayer saves, client save key, map seed, and lobby key.
source_evidence.constraint: Campaign mode needs an explicit custom handshake and cannot require a matching guest legacy save.

source_evidence.observation: SaveGameInfo uses executable game_version, a per-file player_num, players, map messages, and generic additional_data.
source_evidence.constraint: Use a separate campaign envelope with an independent schema and owner.

source_evidence.observation: Session state is populated into SaveGameInfo and written directly as one JSON or binary file.
source_evidence.constraint: Leave legacy saves intact and add a campaign snapshot plus journal beside them.

source_evidence.observation: The server distributes its selected map seed and level transition to clients.
source_evidence.constraint: Authored-event choice and campaign commits remain host-owned.

source_evidence.observation: Clients consume the server-provided seed and load the level.
source_evidence.constraint: Clients consume committed selections and do not select independently.

source_evidence.observation: The engine declares distinct local, synchronized network, map, server-map, and map-sequence RNG streams.
source_evidence.constraint: Event selection gets a fresh domain-separated, selector-versioned RNG instance.

source_evidence.observation: Class setup changes attributes and proficiencies, while session rules can replace or add to those values.
source_evidence.constraint: Class selects a lens; authoritative current capabilities determine action offers.

source_evidence.observation: Runtime Item has established fields plus a runtime UID but no extensible campaign-quality record.
source_evidence.constraint: Unique identity and qualities require an explicit sidecar binding.

source_evidence.observation: newItem allocates a runtime UID and assigns appearance directly.
source_evidence.constraint: Runtime UID is not durable and appearance cannot be repurposed as a campaign key.

source_evidence.observation: The observed item packet carries established item fields and owner UID, not campaign instance data.
source_evidence.constraint: Custom item creation and mutation messages must carry the opaque campaign item ID.

source_evidence.observation: Saved inventory item records contain type, status, appearance, beatitude, count, identification, and grid position.
source_evidence.constraint: Durable qualities live in the host registry and are projected into engine items.

decisions.decision: Add a separate CampaignStateAdapter with a versioned full snapshot, checksum, idempotency receipts, journal, backup, and host-only commit path.
Require matching custom build, campaign protocol, selector version, readable schema, and content manifest before campaign state is sent.
Keep legacy save files and readers unchanged; do not use additional_data or item appearance as the campaign store.
Use class identity for perception and interpretation lenses and current host-derived capabilities for actions.
Select only validated authored definitions using sorted candidates, integer weights, canonical inputs, an isolated versioned RNG seed, and a committed selection ledger.
Store unique item instances in the campaign registry and bind them explicitly to ordinary runtime item projections.

required_invariants: Only the host mutates campaign state.
Every mutation has an opaque operation ID, expected revision, deterministic result, and durable receipt.
Persisted per-actor command sequences and compacted-through high-water marks reject duplicates exactly after full receipt bodies are compacted.
Reconnect receives a visibility-filtered snapshot followed by contiguous ordered deltas.
Host loss pauses the campaign in the initial scope.
No mandatory progression predicate checks for one class.
Every mandatory affordance has a universal in-footprint route and an independent alternate route.
All-same-class four-player parties can reach every essential exit.
Required discoveries are learnable through at least two accessible in-world clue or feedback channels without a wiki, source reading, debug identifiers, or forced lethal trial and error.
Required qualitative progress never depends on repeating an event, farming a resource, kill counts, or a low-probability drop.
Every connected participant receives meaningful contribution opportunities beyond observing synchronized state.
Already committed event choices are replayed and never recalculated.
Event RNG is isolated from layout, combat, loot, presentation, timing, connection order, and unordered iteration.
Every unique item has at least two meaningful qualities in two decision dimensions, including at least one non-scalar verb or system relationship.
Unique item acquisition and lifecycle mutations are idempotent.
Legacy saves are never overwritten or silently converted.
Campaign state and retail assets are never packaged as one distributable payload.

human_feedback_required: each participant's perceived contribution and agency
accessibility against stated needs and observed testing
experience_acceptance.feedback_prompt_scope: what each player noticed, inferred, chose, contributed, and wished they could try without requesting hidden answers

prerequisites: four-player join, transition, disconnect, reconnect, host quit, save, and reload evidence
first_slice: Campaign V1 store and recovery harness
public fixture prepare, select, return, quit, and reload loop

verification_required: seed sweeps for connector, reachability, cooldown, and distribution bounds
fault injection before and after prepare, temporary snapshot flush, authoritative snapshot replacement, journal commit marker, and acknowledgement
receipt compaction with exact rejection of every consumed sequence at or below each actor's persisted high-water mark
duplicate, stale, reordered, and conflicting operation IDs
four peers observing identical committed revisions
unique item acquire, use, transfer or drop, return, reload, reconnect, and duplicate intent

open_risks.summary: Stable direct-connect guest identity and reconnect credential storage are not designed or runtime-tested.
Target filesystems' flush and atomic replacement guarantees are unverified.
Item sidecar integration crosses stacking, shops, followers, containers, death drops, and multiple item packets.
Packet sizing, fragmentation, retries, and transport-specific behavior are unmeasured.
Accessible presentation and privacy of member-specific observations need four-peer runtime tests.
